newsitem.title: CYPRUS: British soldiers plead not guilty to Cyprus assault.
newsitem.headline: British soldiers plead not guilty to Cyprus assault.

text.p: Five British soldiers charged with attacking a group of tourists at a holiday resort in Cyprus last weekend pleaded not guilty on Thursday to three counts of assault.

Soldiers Roger Bell, 26, Tim Carter, 20, Steven Wolstencroft, 26, Steven Girvan, 20, and Stuart Spencer, 20, denied causing grievous and actual bodily harm to three British tourists in the seaside resort of Ayia Napa early on Saturday morning.
The Famagusta district court, sitting in Larnaca, ordered the case be set for hearing on Monday, August 11.
All five soldiers were released into the custody of the British bases authorities on a 2,000 pound ($3,630) bond.
Avoiding the cameras, Spencer, who was detained in connection with the case on Wednesday afternoon, entered and left the courtroom with a dark green beach towel wrapped around his head.
The four other soldiers, all riflemen with the 600-strong Kings Regiment based at Dhekelia, turned their heads away from the cameras as they were escorted out of the courtroom by regimental officers.
The five are charged with attacking the tourists outside a disco in the Ayia Napa resort early on Saturday morning.

Car mechanic Shane Bell, 23, is in a clinic recuperating from an operation on a fractured jaw he suffered during the fight. Quantity surveyor Barry Ford, 23, suffered a shattered right wrist. The third member of the group is Claire Harbour, 22.

It was only one month ago that the British base authorities lifted restrictions on soldiers' visits to the area, first imposed in September 1994 after the brutal killing of a Danish tour guide by three members of the Royal Greenjackets regiment.
Those three soldiers are now serving a life sentence in Cyprus's central prison.
The British base authorities re-imposed the ban on visits to Ayia Napa by members of the Kings regiment after Saturday's incident.
Around 3,500 British troops are stationed at two military bases Britain has retained in Cyprus since independence in 1960. ($=0.55 pounds)
